sources.confirmed: The archived POSIX spawn manual says descriptors remain open unless marked close-on-exec, and file actions can alter their behavior. It is dated August 9, 2007.

sources.title: Per-descriptor close-on-exec control with fcntl
sources.sections_read: Descriptor flags, F_SETFD, F_GETFD, and manual footer
sources.confirmed: The manual defines F_GETFD/F_SETFD close-on-exec controls and states that F_DUPFD creates a descriptor whose close-on-exec flag is clear; its footer is dated January 12, 1994.
sources.limits: A separate flag-setting call leaves a creation-to-flag interval in concurrent programs; a policy must cover every creation and duplication path, and close-on-exec does not itself prevent the initial fork from copying descriptors. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: pre_decision. Original read and any failures remain in runs/B/C11.json.

sources.title: Ordered descriptor actions with posix_spawn
sources.sections_read: Description of ordered spawn file actions; dated footer
sources.confirmed: The dated manual describes an ordered set of child file actions and says descriptors not modified by actions close when FD_CLOEXEC is set.
sources.limits: This only governs launch paths that use the configured spawn call, so it complements descriptor-level flags and cannot by itself protect other launchers or arbitrary external modules. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: pre_decision. Original read and any failures remain in runs/B/C11.json.

sources.title: Atomic close-on-exec file creation with open/openat O_CLOEXEC
sources.version_or_date: Linux man-pages 6.19; page dated 2026-02-08, HTML created 2026-09-09
sources.confirmed: O_CLOEXEC creates a descriptor already marked to close at exec and avoids the race between separate open and fcntl calls; the page identifies Linux 2.6.23 as introduction.
sources.limits: Requires platform support and coverage at each acquisition site; it does not retrofit already-open descriptors, and intended inheritance needs an explicit exception. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: post_decision. Original read and any failures remain in runs/B/C11.json.

sources.title: Close-on-exec descriptor duplication with dup3
sources.version_or_date: Linux man-pages 6.19, page dated 2026-02-08; HTML created 2026-09-09
sources.sections_read: dup/dup2/dup3 behavior, O_CLOEXEC, history and colophon
sources.confirmed: dup and dup2 normally clear close-on-exec on the duplicate; dup3 can request O_CLOEXEC while duplicating. The manual identifies dup3 with Linux 2.6.27/glibc 2.9 but the opened edition is from 2026.
sources.limits: Ordinary dup/dup2 clear the flag on a new duplicate, so callers cannot assume it is shared with the original; intended standard-stream remapping has different inheritance requirements, and dup3 rejects equal source and destination numbers. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: post_decision. Original read and any failures remain in runs/B/C11.json.

sources.title: Close-on-exec pipe creation with pipe2
sources.version_or_date: Linux man-pages 6.19; page dated 2026-02-08, HTML created 2026-09-09
sources.confirmed: pipe2 with O_CLOEXEC sets close-on-exec on both returned pipe descriptors as part of creation; the opened Linux manual edition is dated 2026.
sources.limits: Both endpoints must be considered, and an endpoint intentionally mapped to a child's standard stream must be retained explicitly; unsupported platforms need a different implementation. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: post_decision. Original read and any failures remain in runs/B/C11.json.

sources.title: Close-on-exec socket creation with SOCK_CLOEXEC
sources.version_or_date: Linux man-pages 6.19, page dated 2025-10-29; HTML created 2026-09-09
sources.confirmed: socket accepts SOCK_CLOEXEC in the type flags to mark the new descriptor at creation. The text attributes this facility to Linux 2.6.27, while the opened manual edition is dated 2025.
sources.limits: This covers descriptors created by socket(), not every later socket-producing operation; platform capability checks and intentional descriptor-passing behavior still need a defined policy. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: post_decision. Original read and any failures remain in runs/B/C11.json.
